lensNotes.relies: Outside-in: what each layer provides to you, and the risks if it falters (financial materiality).
lensNotes.affects: Inside-out: what your decisions push onto each layer (impact materiality).

layers.name: Biosphere
layers.summary: Climate, water, land, living systems and the materials we dig up. Its limits are set by physics, chemistry and ecology, not by policy. Seven of the nine planetary boundaries are now breached.
layers.question: Which natural limits does your technology lean on hardest: energy, water, minerals or land?

lenses.name: DIST
lenses.note: for technology's share: digital impacts beyond carbon

layers.name: Society
layers.summary: People, communities and the institutions that hold them together: health, education, rights, work, trust and democracy.
layers.question: Who is affected by your systems without ever choosing to use them?

layers.name: Economy and sectors
layers.summary: Industries, markets, energy grids, supply chains, finance and regulation. Every sector depends on the others, and on the two layers beneath.
layers.question: Which other sectors does yours depend on, and what happens when they are constrained?

lenses.name: Industry reference models
lenses.note: BIAN, TM Forum, HL7 FHIR, IEC CIM

layers.name: Business ecosystem
layers.summary: Customers, suppliers, partners, competitors, regulators and the technology you build on: cloud, SaaS, AI models and open source.
layers.question: Where do you shape the ecosystem through what you buy, build, share and standardise on?

layers.name: Your organisation
layers.summary: Teams, systems, processes, data and decisions. The only layer you control directly, and it rests on everything beneath it.
layers.question: Do you have the feedback loops to see what your decisions do to the layers below, and to respond in time?

sectors.name: Any organisation
sectors.summary: Every organisation runs on digital systems, and every digital system has a physical footprint somewhere beneath it.

biosphere.relies: Electricity for devices, networks and data centres; water for cooling and chip making; minerals in every piece of hardware.
biosphere.affects: Carbon emissions, water stress, e-waste and mining impacts, much of it upstream in hardware supply chains.

society.relies: Skilled people, healthy communities and enough public trust to keep operating.
society.affects: Jobs and skills, accessibility, privacy, and how AI shapes what people see and decide.

economy.relies: Stable energy, working supply chains, capital and predictable regulation.
economy.affects: Demand for compute, hardware and energy, adding to pressure on grids and supply chains.

business.relies: Cloud platforms, SaaS, AI model providers and open source that you do not control.
business.affects: What you buy and standardise on nudges suppliers, partners and competitors.

organisation.relies: Feedback from every layer below, if you have built the loops to hear it.
organisation.affects: Architecture decisions here set what every layer below has to carry.

sectors.name: Financial services
sectors.summary: Your biggest footprint is rarely your own data centres. It is what your money and your models make possible.

biosphere.relies: Reliable power and cooling for trading and core systems; a stable climate underneath loan books and insurance portfolios.
biosphere.affects: Financed emissions usually far exceed operational ones; compute for risk, fraud and AI models adds to the total.

society.relies: Public trust in the system and a skilled, accountable workforce.
society.affects: Who gets credit and on what terms; automated decisions can widen or narrow exclusion.

economy.relies: Market infrastructure, payment networks and stable energy prices.
economy.affects: Capital allocation decides which sectors grow, including the energy and data centre build-out.

business.relies: A few concentrated cloud and platform providers, which is why operational resilience rules focus on third parties.
business.affects: Shared standards such as open banking APIs and BIAN shape how the whole ecosystem integrates.

organisation.relies: Clear accountability for models and for the third parties behind them.
organisation.affects: Architecture choices fix how much compute each product and model consumes for years.

sectors.name: Energy and utilities
sectors.summary: You sit closest to the foundation. Every other sector's digital footprint passes through your networks.

biosphere.relies: Weather for renewables, water for generation and cooling, land for networks and new capacity.
biosphere.affects: Your generation mix sets the carbon intensity of everyone else's electricity, data centres included.

society.relies: Public consent for new infrastructure and a skilled engineering workforce.
society.affects: Affordability, security of supply and the fairness of the transition.

economy.relies: Investment, supply chains for grid equipment and clear policy.
economy.affects: New demand from data centres and electrification competes for the same grid connections.

business.relies: Operational technology vendors, telemetry and forecasting platforms, and a regulator.
business.affects: Data standards such as the Common Information Model shape how the whole system shares data.

organisation.relies: Operational data you can trust, from sensors to settlement.
organisation.affects: Digital decisions in operational systems carry safety, resilience and carbon consequences.

sectors.name: Public sector
sectors.summary: You serve everyone, including people who cannot choose another provider. That raises the bar at every layer.

biosphere.relies: Energy for estates and services, and resilience to flooding and heat.
biosphere.affects: Large device estates and buying power give government real influence over hardware lifecycles.

society.affects: Access to essential services, accessibility, and the fairness of automated decisions.

economy.relies: A healthy supplier market and a national digital skills base.
economy.affects: Procurement and policy shape whole markets, from cloud to AI.

business.relies: A small number of large suppliers and platforms shared across departments.
business.affects: Standards such as the GDS Service Standard set expectations for suppliers and other public bodies.

organisation.relies: Data shared safely across organisational boundaries.
organisation.affects: Legacy and architecture decisions lock in costs and footprints for decades.

sectors.name: Technology and SaaS
sectors.summary: Your product's footprint lives mostly in other people's data centres and on your users' devices.

biosphere.relies: Cloud regions with power and cooling, and hardware made from mined materials.
biosphere.affects: Growth in compute and storage, especially AI features, drives energy, water and hardware demand.

society.relies: Users' trust and a healthy developer and open source community.
society.affects: Design choices shape attention, privacy and wellbeing at scale.

economy.relies: Investment and a market for skilled people.
economy.affects: Your platform changes how your customers' industries operate.

business.relies: Hyperscalers, model providers, and open source maintainers you may not pay.
business.affects: The defaults you ship become your customers' footprint and their lock-in.

organisation.relies: Measurement of what each feature actually costs to run.
organisation.affects: Every default, retention period and model choice multiplies across every customer.

sectors.name: Property and infrastructure
sectors.summary: Buildings and infrastructure last for decades. The digital decisions made around them last almost as long.

biosphere.relies: Land, materials and a stable climate for assets designed to last decades.
biosphere.affects: Materials, land use and building energy, with smart building systems and digital twins layered on top.

society.relies: Communities that accept development and a skilled construction workforce.
society.affects: Where people live and work, and the safety and health of the buildings they use.

economy.relies: Grid connections, finance and construction supply chains.
economy.affects: Demand for grid capacity and materials, which other sectors are competing for too.

business.relies: Contractors, consultants and platforms that hold your asset data.
business.affects: Data standards and contract terms decide what information survives across an asset's life.

organisation.relies: Asset data that survives handovers between owners and contractors.
organisation.affects: Digital choices decide whether asset data helps or hinders decarbonisation.
